paper_metadata.title: Effects of cryomilling on the microstructures and high temperature mechanical properties of oxide dispersion strengthened steel

evidence.quote: The effects of cryomilling on the microstructures and high temperature mechanical properties of oxide dispersion-strengthened (ODS) steel were examined.
The existence of secondary phases is evidence that ODS materials are very sensitive to not only process conditions such as milling temperatures, but also contamination.

In the present study, the microstructures and high-temperature mechanical (compression) properties of ODS steels manufactured through MA under the cooling conditions of RT (K1) and 0150 C (K4) were examined

If stress is imposed at high temperatures, grain boundary sliding and intergranular fractures will be caused.

some secondary phases located on grain boundaries such as W carbide can act as nuclei of cavity formation and have incidental effects on grain boundary weakening. Therefore, these causes of grain boundary weakening are thought to have acted in combination so that the strength of the K4 was degraded at high temperatures and intergranular fractures occurred in compression specimens under all temperature conditions.
Therefore, the unique fracture surface of the K4 is thought to be a type of intergranular fracture, and the modes of the intergranular fractures are judged to vary according to temperature.
